subject: Price equivalence request and ops handoff for Evergent
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <amorgan@evergent.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 04 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor parity request — Evergent -> Redwood proposal

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency numbers and the control plane. Our procurement lead has asked for a formal price equivalence request to evaluate a switch from CloudForge.

Quick context: we have a negotiated blended rate with CloudForge that includes a modest onboarding credit for the first 3 months and a 9-month committed consumption tier. I attached the current pricing summary and the incumbent SOW excerpt for your reference.

What we need from Redwood to advance:
- A written price-equivalence confirmation (line item comparatives + list of any features not included)
- A proposed onboarding credit or pilot concession (volume + timing)
- A short technical ops handoff plan for the pilot (hours, roles, runbook scope)

If possible, can you share a one-page comparison and a draft SOW by EOD Thursday? Lance (cc'd) will review legal items.

Appreciate it —
Alex

[Attachment: Evergent_current_pricing.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <amorgan@evergent.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 04 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor parity request — Evergent -> Redwood proposal

Alex — thanks for the clear ask. I pulled a quick comparison and started a draft SOW; attaching both. High level response below so your procurement and legal teams have something to react to quickly.

Summary (first pass):
- Price: we can match incumbent per-token/throughput economics for the first 9 months on a committed usage plan, subject to a short technical validation (3-week pilot).
- Onboarding credit: we can offer a $75k onboarding credit applied as bill-back for the first 90 days (structured as a ramp credit, not a rebate).
- Feature parity: Redwood supports all required endpoints; two items to note — 1) dedicated on-prem connector requires our Private deployment agreement (optional), 2) custom telemetry export will be scoped as professional services (estimated 8-12 hrs).

Ops handoff (pilot):
- Pilot window: 3 weeks
- Redwood owners: Connor (technical lead), Monica (onboard PM)
- Deliverables: deployment checklist, KV cache priming plan, latency/SLO baseline report, runbook with rollback steps
- Estimated effort: 24h engineering + 12h onboarding PM + 8h CS training = ~44 person-hours

Next steps I propose:
1) Review attached comparison sheet and SOW draft with your procurement/legal (Lance).
2) If OK, sign the pilot SOW (attached) and book an ops kickoff — Connor will propose slots.
3) We’ll finalize the pricing Annex post pilot and then commit to the 9-month rate.

I attached: Evergent_Comparison_Sheet.xlsx, SOW_draft_Evergent_v2.pdf.

Does Thursday EOD for the comparison + SOW work for you, or do you need earlier?

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim

Date: Sun, 04 Oct 2026 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor parity request — Evergent -> Redwood proposal

Looping in technical notes from my side — I reviewed Evergent's incumbent line items and the attached comparison. A few operational clarifications before we finalize the SOW: 

Pilot/Onboard checklist (ops view):
- Baseline benchmarking: 2-day run against representative traffic (10k requests/day) to validate latency; we’ll produce token-level breakdowns and tail-percentile metrics.
- KV cache strategy: if Evergent uses long chat sessions, we’ll enable prefix caching; cost delta is minimal but reduces latency — call it out as optional.
- Model variants: we should pilot on the 1x replica of the open model that maps closest to their current stack; fallback path to smaller quantized model if capacity constrained.
- Egress & compliance: confirm whether logs need to be forwarded to their SIEM (if so, we’ll add 4-6hrs to PS).

Estimated engineering time: 24 hours for baseline + 12 hours for runbook + 8 hours for integration support. I can staff this week of Oct 12 if the pilot kickoffs then.

If everyone agrees on these bullets I’ll update the SOW task list and add a short annex covering caching and fallback routing.

—Connor
Connor O'Brien
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 04 Oct 2026 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor parity request — Evergent -> Redwood proposal

Alex/Lance — attaching an updated SOW draft that incorporates Connor's ops checklist and a short annex on caching/fallback. Two quick clarifications from our side before you circulate to procurement: 

- The onboarding credit ($75k) will be invoiced as a negative line on month 1 and amortized across the first 3 billing cycles. This keeps your accounting simple and preserves the committed-rate structure.
- Feature exceptions: telemetry export to a third-party SIEM is treated as a billable PS item; we left an optional line in the SOW with an hours estimate.

If this looks good to legal, please sign the pilot SOW (DocuSign link below) and we’ll schedule an ops kickoff with Connor next Tuesday/Wednesday. I’ll also open a HubSpot deal and link the pricing Annex.

DocuSign: https://docusign.example.com/start/EVG-2026-119
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/EVG-2026-119

Thanks — I’ll block time for a 30-minute kickoff once you confirm the signature.

Rachel
